The corpus holds 67,293 tokens in English and 60,026 in Arabic. Three models were tested, with GPT-4o-mini scoring highest at 37.07 BLEU, showing the corpus's discriminative power.
arxiv-2604-00115: Syzranov and Ramirez point out a practical sign of zero-point entropy in higher-temperature magnetic data. It is the entropy frozen into a material at absolute zero. If it is wrongly assumed absent, a Maxwell relation linking entropy, field, magnetization, and temperature can look broken, and that false break itself gives an estimate of the missing entropy. Below set temperatures the test boils down to a sign check on two rates of change, shown here on the well-known spin ice dysprosium titanate.
arxiv-2604-00215: Ravish Gupta, Kumar, and Dang build an agentic AI framework for crowded Indian outpatient departments, where first-come-first-served tokens ignore urgency. Six parts cover voice symptom capture, severity prediction, physician assignment, queue optimization with drift detection, an orchestrator, and patient memory. Simulated runs at a Jabalpur District Hospital, 368 patients over 30 runs, see 94.2 percent of critical patients within 10 minutes, against 30.8 percent under first-come-first-served. It spots about 236 drift events per session and about 12 hidden-critical cases, shifting queues toward critical and high urgency at 40 patients per hour.
arxiv-2604-00515: Wang and Zhang test a quantum version of Oppenheimer-Snyder black holes as primordial black holes that could make up all dark matter. Primordial holes are popular dark-matter candidates. They are usually drawn as Schwarzschild or Kerr holes, which carry curvature singularities at their centres. Quantum-gravity fixes may remove the singularity and leave a different spacetime shape. The authors find their corrected holes run at temperatures and greybody factors far from the Schwarzschild values. That gap damps Hawking emission and eases gamma-ray constraints.
arxiv-2604-00715: Singh and colleagues study scaling laws for retrieval-aware pretraining: memorise or retrieve? Retrieval-augmented generation improves language models by supplying context at test time for hard knowledge tasks. The team studies the training-retrieval trade-off, training OLMo-2-based models from 30 million to 3 billion parameters on 100 billion DCLM tokens, varying data scale, store size, and source across three QA benchmarks. Retrieval gains depend on capacity and pretraining history and come mostly early, with a median 91 percent of the largest improvement realised by one token per parameter.
arxiv-2604-00815: Luu and colleagues fix precision loss in determinant quantum Monte Carlo at low temperatures, where evaluating the fermion determinant and its inverse grows unstable. Using varied matrix decompositions, they push simulations to inverse temperature at least 90. That is the room-temperature regime for graphene structures, for both plain determinant methods and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo variants. Their implementation costs about the same as the naive version, scaling with the cube of spatial sites times time sites.
arxiv-2604-00915: Ma and team introduce LT-O-learners, orthogonal learners for estimating heterogeneous long-term treatment effects from combined short-term and long-term data. Thin overlap in treatment assignments or long-term outcomes for some groups can destabilize estimates. Their key idea retargets the loss with custom overlap weights that downweight low-overlap samples, recovering the true effect pointwise with Neyman-orthogonality. They prove nuisance error enters only through higher-order terms and retargeting controls asymptotic variance in low-overlap regimes, then confirm both on synthetic and real data.
arxiv-2604-01115: Richardson and colleagues rework polynomial PDEs through their highest spatial derivative. That derivative, called the fundamental state, lives in L2 with no boundary rules. For polynomial cases they express that state's motion as a spread-out polynomial under a new tensor algebra of integral operators. They then build a sum-of-squares form of that polynomial and use it to test local stability of polynomial PDEs.
arxiv-2604-01215: Garg and colleagues build one math framework for AI weather prediction that covers the whole learning pipeline, not architecture alone. Using approximation theory, dynamical systems, information theory, and statistical learning, they split pipeline error and show error from loss and data beats error from design at current scales. They also formalize spectral blurring from mean-square loss and bound how data-driven models underestimate record-breaking extremes. Empirical tests back these predictions.
arxiv-2604-01415: Hanson studies non-positively curved closed manifolds and their n-dimensional totally geodesic submanifolds in the product M by M, under transversality. He proves that, under mild irreducibility on M, infinitely many such ones force M to be a locally symmetric space. A single dense one forces the same result. His proof gives a stronger version needing such ones only in the universal cover product.
arxiv-2604-01515: Almeida asks what controls quantum Fisher information at band-touching defects: spatial dimensionality, band structure, or a geometric property of the defect. He shows the singular contribution to the quantum Fisher information with respect to the tuning parameter m obeys a power-law scaling. The exponent is p minus 2, where p is the codimension, except at p equals 2, where a logarithmic divergence appears. The result unifies SSH chains, Chern insulators, and Weyl semimetals as one codimension class, and shows that only defects with p at most 2 generate responses.
arxiv-2604-01715: Dao and colleagues present SteerFlow, a framework for text-guided image editing by inversion, which often loses fidelity. Methods lose fidelity: solvers add calls, truncated inversion limits edits, and feature injection rarely transfers. SteerFlow straightens the path with a fixed-point solver enforcing velocity consistency across steps, yielding an inverted latent. Trajectory Interpolation blends target and source velocities to anchor edits, while Adaptive Masking narrows the edit signal with concept segmentation. Tests on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and FLUX.1-dev show better editing quality, and multi-turn edits avoid drift.
arxiv-2604-02115: Yang and Mao settle a 2010 conjecture of Butler, Costello and Graham on monochromatic constellations. A constellation is a finite rational pattern scaled and shifted inside a range, with arithmetic progressions as a key example. The claim was that some coloring scheme always yields fewer of these patterns than random coloring would. The authors prove it for every pattern. The proof yields new linear systems and a spin system bound.
arxiv-2604-02715: Liu and six colleagues present FluxMoE, a serving system that frees mixture-of-experts models from keeping every expert on the GPU at once. Existing engines crowd out the key-value cache in large offline jobs by holding all experts resident. FluxMoE pages experts on demand through a bandwidth-balanced hierarchy of compressed GPU memory and host DRAM. On GLM-4.5 it reaches up to 7.2 times the throughput of vLLM with no measurable quality loss.
arxiv-2604-02915: Kim, Kim and Han present GP-4DGS, a framework adding Gaussian processes to 4D splatting for probabilistic modeling of dynamic scenes from monocular video. Fixed methods miss unclear motion and cannot judge prediction trust. Their approach adds uncertainty measures for motion, motion estimates for unseen or sparse regions, and forecasts beyond training frames. Space-time kernels plus variational Gaussian processes with inducing points make inference doable. Tests show better rebuilt scenes with reliable uncertainty readings. The work bridges probabilistic modeling and neural graphics.
arxiv-2604-03315: Li and colleagues build StoryBlender, a 3D storyboard system that keeps characters and scenes consistent across shots while staying directly editable. A three-stage pipeline grounds story and space, places assets in one coordinate frame, and designs layout and motion over time, with agents checking and fixing spatial errors. Tests show it beats both diffusion-based and 3D-grounded baselines on consistency and editability.
arxiv-2604-03515: Rombaut presents a source-code-level map of coding agent designs, drawn from 13 open-source agent scaffolds at pinned commits. Each agent is scored across 12 axes in three layers: control design, tool and setting links, and resource handling. Control plans resist discrete sorting, spanning fixed pipelines and Monte Carlo Tree Search, and 11 of 13 agents combine more than one loop building block rather than leaning on one control structure.
arxiv-2604-03815: Jonas De Schouwer and colleagues built k-Maximum Inner Product attention, a sparse attention pattern for graph transformers that picks only the top-k keys per query. Full attention costs quadratic memory, while linearized and restricted variants often lose power. Their design runs in linear memory, speeds up work by up to an order of magnitude, and handles graphs over 500,000 nodes on one A100 GPU. Theory shows it can approximate full attention arbitrarily well.
arxiv-2604-04215: Jingyi Yang and team presented DARE, an open framework for post-training and testing diffusion language models. The open-source world for these models is fragmented across families and post-training pipelines, slowing work and fair tests. Built on verl and OpenCompass, DARE unifies supervised fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, preference optimization, and diffusion reinforcement learning under one execution stack for masked and block models. Broad tests across LLaDA, Dream, SDAR, and LLaDA2.x models mark DARE as a reusable base for building, comparing, and shipping post-training methods.
arxiv-2604-04415: Li and colleagues introduce Structured Event Evidence, a unified time-ordered schema for video reasoning. Training a model to pull evidence while reasoning creates a bottleneck: rollouts must meet schema, accuracy and budget. Standard reinforcement learning uses static weights, forcing a rigid accuracy-length trade-off. Group-Relative Advantage Balancing sets Pareto-optimal weights per rollout group from centered rewards, with near-zero overhead and no brittle tuning. As PARSE-4B on PARSE-60K, it uses 13 to 39 percent fewer tokens while matching tuned weights on grounding and question-answering.
arxiv-2604-04515: Mahmudi and colleagues launch CommonMorph, a site easing morphological data work via rules, user prompts and crowd checks. Getting and tagging word data takes linguistic skill, care and resources, hitting small tongues hardest. The site cuts hand work with learning, annotation hints and tools to bring in and tweak kin-tongue stuff. It copes with varied word systems such as fusional, agglutinative and root-and-pattern forms. Its free design and UniMorph-ready outputs keep it open and interoperable with NLP tools, giving a model for saving diversity.
arxiv-2604-04715: Merino, for the Fermilab Lattice and MILC Collaborations, reviews efforts toward a precision test of first row CKM unitarity from lattice QCD. High-precision Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix elements probe physics beyond the Standard Model. At current precision, only Vud and Vus contribute to this test. Without nuclear inputs, they come from kaon and pion leptonic decay widths plus theoretical decay constants. They also use semileptonic kaon decay width plus the zero-momentum form factor. The review covers the collaborations' correlated analysis of lattice inputs using Highly Improved Staggered Quarks.
arxiv-2604-04915: Dongre and five colleagues probe how wearable stress alerts could pair with chatbot support for daily stress care. Their EmBot app joins wearable-triggered stress detection to language-model conversation, then serves as a design probe in interviews with 15 mental health experts. The experts surface tensions in timing, trust, and tone when a device ping launches a supportive chat. Those early design lessons aim to guide future systems that link body signals to dialogue without overstepping clinical care.
arxiv-2604-05215: Xiong and 10 colleagues give a net tool for analysis that runs on tree splits built from shapes. The design handles volume and surface grids in one build, giving focus without tweaks. A mapping module maps tags into the tree, splitting shape from feature size. Training via masked rebuild of points and channels on raw cohorts yields a shared encoder for tasks and types. On dementia tests and amyloid guessing with ADNI meshes, and flaw spotting on MELD meshes, it hits the best results.
arxiv-2604-05415: Wang and five colleagues segment wheat disease from scarce training images, where disease appearance shifts across growth stages and full datasets are impractical to collect. Their SGPer framework pairs DINOv2 semantic priors with SAM geometric priors: disease-tuned adapters align both models, dense prompts propose disease regions, and confidence filtering trims them. Evaluations report leading performance on wheat disease and organ benchmarks, especially with little data.
arxiv-2604-05615: Bshouty and Haddad extend constant-query testability to new Boolean function classes. For k-juntas, low Fourier-degree functions, and sparse polynomials, testing costs a number of queries inversely proportional to epsilon when epsilon is small, independent of variable count. Any properly exactly learnable class depending on few variables inherits the same testability.
arxiv-2604-05715: Xiao and six colleagues make single-camera depth clues safe for 3D Gaussian Splatting, where scale mix-ups and view clashes otherwise spoil renders. Their setup learns from loosely lined-up depth shifts and fences off ill-posed shapes for picked depth control, shielding well-built forms. Tests across data sets and backbones show steadier shapes and crisper renders.
arxiv-2604-06115: Wang strengthens a weak Galerkin finite element method for elliptic problems of second order whose solutions are rough or singular. The method adds neural network functions chosen by a residual-driven enrichment step to the classical approximation space, keeping its variational structure, symmetry, and stability. Wang proves a near-optimal error bound in a discrete energy norm and shows smooth solutions still converge at the optimal rate. For problems splitting into smooth and singular parts, the neural enrichment captures the singular part and beats standard weak Galerkin accuracy.
arxiv-2604-06415: Todowede adapts earthquake hazard math to frequency risk in Probabilistic Frequency Hazard Analysis. Falling synchronous inertia leaves frequency open to supply and interconnector shocks; methods lack risk measures and hazard curves. His hazard integral covers loss sources, shock sizes, and grid states through a formula with aleatory spread. From 51 sources, with epistemic gaps handled by a 324-path tree, it matches the Frequency Risk and Control Report within one and a half times at 49.2 hertz, and sizes cuts from the Dynamic Containment control and the Low-Frequency Demand Disconnection control.
arxiv-2604-06515: Chowdhury and six colleagues assign different precisions to experts in sparse mixture-of-experts models, where only a few experts fire per input yet memory stays heavy. Their theory-backed rule keys bit-width mainly to how much each expert's router norm shifted during training. Steadier experts carry rare but critical features and suffer most from coarse quantization, so they stay precise, as do high-variance experts. On Switch Transformer and Mixtral it beat existing methods while trimming inference cost with negligible assignment overhead.
arxiv-2604-07015: Guzman-Landa and six colleagues ask whether data copying can help language work for low-resource tongues. Such pi-tongues have almost no corpora for language models. The team studies Nawatl, a glue-like pi-language spoken by millions, growing the pi-yalli corpus by copying. Static vectors on the grown corpus were tested on sentence meaning match, showing some gain over no growth. The authors note step-by-step copying appears unused in books.
arxiv-2604-07315: Sattar, Stepanov, and Canali study magneto-optical switching in even-layered films of MnBi2Te4, a material where magnetism and topology intertwine. Using a Dirac-cone model plus tight-binding calculations, they show that the spin alignment of the outer layers chiefly controls the Chern number and optical response. Flipping a six-layer film's outer alignment from antiparallel to parallel switches it from an axion insulator with no Faraday rotation to a Chern insulator with a quantized response. Thicker films add a further phase with Chern number 2.
arxiv-2604-07415: Petcu, Kanoulas, and de Rijke introduce SubSearch, which rewards mid-reasoning steps for hard retrieval instead of grading only final answers. Hard queries need multi-step reasoning over retrieved facts with no preset path, and outcome-only training leaves that path unshaped. SubSearch tunes the generator directly with intrinsic process rewards built into the system, needing no human-labeled paths or large-model judges. On seven benchmarks, intrinsic mid-step rewards give sturdier reasoning traces than outcome rewards alone.
arxiv-2604-07515: Blelloch and four colleagues develop the efficient algorithm for keeping an independent set under parallel batch updates. Graphs update by adds and drops, and a joint algorithm refreshes the set. Efficiency means low work plus polylog depth. For a batch of b updates, their algorithm needs order b log cubed n mean work and polylog depth usually, beating the best serial dynamic methods. The analysis builds a batch influence-set approach, since batch influence is not just the union of single-update effects.
arxiv-2604-07615: Arora and three colleagues introduce ADAG, a fully auto tool for describing attribution graphs in circuit tracing. Past circuit tracing relied on ad-hoc human reading of each feature role from firing cases. ADAG scores each feature role with attribution cards from input and output slope effects, groups features by similarity, and uses a writer-tester setup to generate and score plain-language notes. On known human-studied tasks, the system recovers clear circuits. It also finds steered clusters behind a harmful advice jailbreak in the Llama 3.1 Instruct model.
arxiv-2604-07815: Hu and nine colleagues speed up long-context language-model inference with AsyncTLS, a two-level sparse attention system. Coarse block filtering first narrows the field, then fine token selection picks precisely, balancing accuracy against cost. An async offload engine overlaps transfers of stored key-value data with computation, using temporal locality. On Qwen3 and GLM-4.7-Flash, accuracy stays close to full attention. Operator speedups reach up to tenfold and end-to-end throughput gains up to nearly fivefold on contexts of 48,000 to 96,000 tokens.
arxiv-2604-08115: Shim, Hong, and Lim present Revise, a framework fixing OCR errors in real document systems. Large language models boosted Document AI on tasks like question answers. Current methods focus on single tasks and lack the ability to order and manage document information. Revise corrects errors from optical text reading at letter, word, and shape levels. It uses a hierarchical taxonomy of common OCR errors plus a synthetic data plan that mimics such errors to train a fixer model. Tests show Revise corrects OCR outputs well, giving more tidy form.
arxiv-2604-08315: Zhang and three colleagues unify topological, geometric, and complex black hole thermodynamics schemes. Black hole thermodynamics lately saw three schemes: from local temperature shapes, global topological invariants, and complex-plane Riemann foliations. They show these schemes map onto one another via two dictionaries. One ties thermal stability to temperature-curve trends; the other ties black hole state counts to Riemann surface foliation numbers. Extremal points of the temperature curve set the scheme in all frames, rooting this link in key points of the solution space.
arxiv-2604-08515: Chapple and three colleagues map state jumps caused by measurement across the fluxonium qubit landscape, where multi photon resonances leak population from working states to higher states during readout. Lighter fluxoniums prove less vulnerable, thanks to sparser resonances, smaller coupling needs, and a more harmonic charge operator structure. Time dependent readout simulations confirm the picture, and the study also weighs effects from the superinductor's array modes.
arxiv-2604-08915: Fan and seven colleagues build a large foundation model for creating defect images, the flawed examples used to train inspection systems. Earlier few-shot methods overfit narrow defect types because paired examples of normal and damaged parts were scarce, and varied defect sizes and shapes made the problem worse. Their UDG collection holds 300,000 normal, damaged, mask, and caption quadruples across many domains. Their UniDG model trains in two stages, first for variety and then for consistency, and it beats prior methods on standard benchmarks and on downstream detection tasks.
arxiv-2604-09115: Hou, Yu, and Wu present Wi2SAR, a self-flying drone for wilderness search and rescue through cover, without standing networks. The insight is that Wi-Fi devices rejoin known networks on their own, so a drone copying those networks can find victims through their phones. Three ideas make it usable: fast, thrifty search; long-range bearing from signal strength alone using a 3D-printed Luneburg lens; and smart steering to the target. A test unit tried across devices and field settings shows strong results and low power use.
arxiv-2604-09215: Partmann, Wieners, Ortiz, and Weinberg introduce phase-field peridynamics, a fracture model that avoids deleting bonds. Peridynamics writes momentum balance as one equation, suiting fracture without special handling of cracks. Yet deleting bonds step by step degrades the gradient and can cause instability. Instead, each bond's energy is degraded continuously through a phase-field parameter, while a separate function keeps the gradient accurate. Tests on mode I and II fracture confirm stability and accuracy.
arxiv-2604-09515: Ashik and four colleagues test how language models write code when software libraries keep changing underneath them, assembling 270 real updates from eight Python libraries and running them across 11 models. Without full documentation, models produce runnable code in the target setup only about 43 percent of the time, since stale memorized patterns override new specifications. Structured documentation and larger models lift that rate to about 66 percent, and self-reflection improves it by 11 percent, yet outdated habits persist.
arxiv-2604-09715: Markhorst and four co-authors present MuPPet, a multi-person 2D-to-3D pose-lifting method that models ties between people. Current lifting methods neglect inter-person ties or fail as group sizes vary. MuPPet encodes each person, diversifies training through Permutation Augmentation, and adapts correlation modeling through Dynamic Multi-Person Attention. Tests on group datasets show it beating leading single- and multi-person methods and staying robust under occlusion.
arxiv-2604-09915: Macovei, Richter, and Pálffy investigate quantum dynamics of driven nuclear two-level systems in a leaky broadband cavity, pumped by two x-ray fields. When both applied fields share a frequency, cross-correlations among decay channels raise nuclear excitation odds depending on the fields' phase difference. The excited ensemble shows sub- to super-Poissonian statistics, showing induced correlations during photon absorption or emission. Cross-correlations also shape the ensemble's superradiant decay and collective Lamb shift.
arxiv-2604-10215: Townsend and Wang show oblivious subspace injection alone does not guarantee relative-error bounds. It is weaker than embedding yet gives constant bounds for sketch-and-solve least squares. Asked at a 2025 Simons Institute workshop whether it implies error bounds, the team answers no, with counter-cases for least squares and random SVD. Failure chance cannot be set by the injection failure value, though such sketches often perform well. The missing piece is control on the leftover; with that trait, a near bound follows.
arxiv-2604-10315: Deb, Beige, and Clark show Bell-CHSH tests, good for spatial links, are mostly too weak for time links. They build classic and quantum finite state makers from one bit and one qubit, matching time links in output strings. For paired reads by two watchers, classic boxes can pass the Tsirelson bound by structure. With a time delay between paired reads, quantum boxes beat classic ones, holding links longer under scrambling moves. The result can tell quantum from classic tasks and point to new quantum tools.
arxiv-2604-10715: Zhang and four colleagues defend neural networks against patch-based and texture-based adversarial attacks, the physically realizable kind that threatens surveillance and autonomous systems. Their Adversarial Spectrum Defense uses discrete wavelet transforms to split attack patterns across frequency scales, capturing both fine-grained high-frequency and pervasive low-frequency changes. Combined with adversarial training, the method beats prior defenses by 21.73 percent in average precision against strong adaptive adversaries built to defeat it. It sets a new state of the art for both attack types.
arxiv-2604-10815: Xu presents MeloTune, an iPhone music agent running Mesh Memory Protocol and Symbolic-Vector Attention Fusion for curation and mood coupling. Each device runs two continuous-time networks: a private network guessing mood paths, and a shared network mixing memory blocks. Hidden states never cross the wire; only memory blocks do. A personal arousal function swaps the linear map from audio loudness to arousal with a learned tweak trained on behavior and drift. The model hits path error 0.414, pattern scores 96.6 percent, and intent scores 69.4 percent on held-out tests.
arxiv-2604-11015: Matsui constructs quantum many-body systems hosting an invariant scar subspace. This extends quantum many-body scars beyond equal spacing and tower structures. Construction rests on constraints realizing algebraic closure within the scar subspace. The spectrum there is no longer equally spaced but forms a multidirectional lattice set by several quantum numbers. Instead of single revivals, the system shows multifrequency oscillations governed by integer combinations of energy scales. Scar stability does not rely on solvability of individual eigenstates. Algebraic closure preserves the subspace under perturbations making eigenstates intractable.
arxiv-2604-11315: Ghriss introduces S3, the Structured Sparsity Specification, an algebraic framework for setting up and using structured sparse patterns in tensors. Sparsity is set through a View that reshapes the tensor, a Block that defines the atomic pruning unit, and a Scope that decides where sparsity applies. Coupling across tensors allows coordinated pruning. The point is one language for many pruning styles, from fine N:M patterns to coarse channel cuts. Built entirely on S3, structured OBS and OBD implementations beat established second-order rules on output rebuilds across common setups.
arxiv-2604-11415: Xie and six colleagues tackle cost-aware remote sensing, where low-resolution imagery covers the globe cheaply but high-resolution detail costs dearly and covers little. Existing sampling picks from isolated low-resolution patches, ignoring fine-grained importance within patches and context across them. Their unified formulation couples fine-grained high-resolution sampling with cross-patch representation prediction, reasoning better with fewer costly observations. They also release GL-10M, a dataset of nearly 100,000 scene pairs and 10 million images. Experiments on recognition and retrieval show a superior performance-cost trade-off.
arxiv-2604-11515: Soneji, Crampin, and Mucha-Kruczynski study electronic behavior at graphite junctions, where layer stacking decides the low-energy physics. Interrupted rhombohedral stacking hosts edge-localized topological states, while Bernal stacking does not. Using charge self-consistent tight-binding methods with embedding potentials, they find junction-localized states nearly everywhere. All but one rhombohedral system supports a flat band prone to instabilities and strongly correlated states. Nascent flat-band states from finite rhombohedral sequences extend the physics into pure Bernal systems.
arxiv-2604-11715: Cho and Sowers pose learning Koopman eigenfunctions from observations at uneven, possibly non-vanishing, time gaps as an optimization task. Study shows aliasing from wavy dynamics and sampling patterns, a built-in limit on identification. It also finds phase alignment near the true Koopman frequency, creating a steep loss valley that needs careful tuning. Uneven sampling can break aliasing and cause phase cancellation. Tests show it works under large regular time gaps versus generator extended dynamic mode decomposition, backing uneven sampling for finding the true Koopman spectrum.
arxiv-2604-11815: Morales-Zapien, Jaikumar, and Klähn study how temperature shifts compositional g-modes in the cores of inviscid neutron stars. Using a chiral sigma model, they build isentropic temperature profiles for hot, dense matter. They find the global core g-mode frequency's temperature dependence is governed by the nuclear symmetry energy slope, denoted L. A warm star's mode may therefore run higher or lower than its cold counterpart, so observed g-modes could constrain how symmetry energy varies with density.
arxiv-2604-11915: Gupta and Adami warn that machine-learning life detectors, trained on Earth-like organic mixtures to separate biotic from abiotic samples, are easily fooled. Using artificial life systems, they show such methods report life with near 100 percent confidence for samples incapable of life. The flaw is sensitivity to out-of-distribution inputs: alien samples will almost surely fall outside the training range. Life detection by AI, they conclude, is likely to yield many false positives.
arxiv-2604-12615: Lev Sorokin and two colleagues report the first DeepTest competition on LLM testing. The contest ran at the ICSE 2026 workshop. Four tools benchmarked a car manual assistant built on a language model. The goal was to find inputs where the system omits manual warnings. Tools were scored on failure exposure and test diversity. The report covers method, competitors, and results. It sets a baseline for testing language-model assistants in cars.
arxiv-2604-12715: Filippo Mantovani and 38 colleagues present EPAC, a RISC-V accelerator chip from Europe's processor initiative. The chip uses 22FDX technology and spans 27 square millimeters. It holds about 0.3 billion transistors. Three tiles target distinct workloads: VEC for HPC work, STX for stencil and machine learning, and VRP for iterative solvers. A coherent hub network links the tiles with a distributed cache. External memory connects via a SerDes link. The chip taped out with all major blocks validated. The paper also reflects on lessons from a multi-partner effort across Europe.
arxiv-2604-12815: Miklós Rásonyi proves ergodicity for the SAGA-LD sampling algorithm. SAGA-LD draws samples for machine learning from high-dimensional distributions. Its tangled dynamics resist standard Markov chain theory. A model-specific method shows the chain converges to a limiting distribution. A law of large numbers holds as well.
arxiv-2604-12915: Farhangi, Moreira, and Zelada build a unified ergodic theory framework from Parreau's 2005 construction. That construction finds a nontrivial factor, disjoint from every strongly mixing system, inside any system that is not strongly mixing. They define systems generated by, and mixing relative to, a set of ultrafilters. They prove the two notions are dual through disjointness, and show every partially rigid system is a finite extension of such a generated system.
arxiv-2604-13115: Svinin presents and studies a new infinite family of homogeneous discrete equations with the Laurent property. Every solution remains a Laurent polynomial rather than a general rational function. The first member of the family is the well-known Somos-5 recurrence, anchoring the broader class in a known example, with later members following the same Laurent pattern.
arxiv-2604-14115: Kawasaki, Gao, and Scuseria extend a geminal power framework for quantum chemistry by adding correlations between electron pairs. To keep the new wave functions workable, they rewrite them as combinations of simpler geminal states whose overlaps and energy terms follow standard machinery. Tests on a model lattice and on water and nitrogen molecules show steady high accuracy, beating the simpler combination most clearly for larger systems and strongly correlated regimes.
arxiv-2604-14315: Lugos and Gruppi track how news reports on violent and catastrophic events change over time across 126,602 articles from online publishers. They measure story change through publication volume, semantic drift, semantic spread, and term relevance. Sudden high-impact events show structured, predictable cycles: rapid coverage surges, early semantic drift, and gradual falls toward baseline. Their results also name the terms driving the temporal patterns.
arxiv-2604-14515: Wei, Chen, Tang, and Deng study dual-mode ground-state cooling in a quadratic optomechanical system with one cavity, one linearly coupled resonator, and one quadratically coupled resonator. Tuning detuning and couplings moves the system from optical bistability into multistability with up to seven steady states. Simultaneous ground-state cooling of both resonators occurs on the stable branch, and robust joint cooling holds broadly. The exception comes when linear and quadratic couplings match and a dark mode appears, but tuning second-order frequency shifts suppresses that interference.
arxiv-2604-14715: Bi and Li give uniform volume estimates for balls under a large class of Carnot-Carathéodory distances on generalized Heisenberg-type groups. They also prove weak (1, 1) estimates of order C to the m times n for associated centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal functions. A uniform volume-doubling property for Heisenberg groups under left-invariant Riemannian metrics falls out as a by-product. The results extend earlier work, covering a broad family of distances and metrics in one stroke.
arxiv-2604-14815: Luisto and seven others continued pretraining FinBERT, the Finnish BERT model, on unlabeled Finnish histopathology reports. Training-loss curves differed strongly by domain, a signal worth noting for practitioners. Since the reports carry no classification labels, the team tested whether pretraining signals track downstream gains using public Finnish datasets as proxies. In exploratory analysis, certain pretraining-derived features did correlate with proxy classification improvement. The report adds to the thin literature on natural language processing for Finnish healthcare data.
arxiv-2604-15015: Niu, Zheng, and Ma analyze doubly heavy quarkonium from top decays in nonrelativistic QCD. They study 1 to 4 decay producing (b c-bar) or (c c-bar) plus two quarks, in dominant color-singlet S-wave states. Production yields 10^4 to 10^6 B-c events and 10^3 to 10^5 charmonium events yearly at the LHC. The channel dominates eta-c and J/psi via top decays, testing the narrow-width approximation.
arxiv-2604-15115: Yang and colleagues harden federated learning against Byzantine attackers with FedIDM, built for fast, stable convergence. Earlier robust methods wobble and, under many colluding malicious clients, trade model quality for safety. FedIDM builds trustworthy condensed data through distribution matching, then rejects local updates that stray from its direction or spike its loss. Tests on three benchmarks show fast, stable convergence while keeping model quality acceptable.
arxiv-2604-15515: Veselinov proves an extremal density result for forbidden configurations in S-smooth numbers, sets of integers whose prime factors all lie in a finite set S. The largest subset of S-smooth numbers up to X avoids every scaled set of the form n, p1 n, through pr n. It holds all but about one in r plus one of them. The gap is at most a logarithmic error term. The classical case S equals 2 and 3 yields an explicit tail formula and two structural results for optimal sets.
arxiv-2604-15815: Kersbergen and colleagues introduce a coupled-channels method for elastic three-body scattering among identical bosonic alkali-metal atoms. It rests on an exact two-body transition matrix built from real molecular potentials. Its main output, the complex three-body hypervolume, plays the role for three bodies that the scattering length plays for two. Applied to spin-polarized potassium-39, the method yields the hypervolume with controlled numerical accuracy and should transfer to other atomic species.
arxiv-2604-16015: De Schoulepnikoff and three colleagues show interpretable machine learning can extract physical insight from complex quantum data. Building on variational autoencoders, their models learn representations from unlabeled quantum datasets, revealing structure in quantum phase spaces from raw data alone. Adding symbolic methods yields compact analytical descriptors that act as order parameters for regimes in the representations. Tests on Rydberg-atom snapshots, cluster Ising shadows, and fermionic data reveal a previously unreported corner-ordering pattern in Rydberg arrays. All methods ship in qdisc, an open-source Python library.
arxiv-2604-16215: Corrêa and Massarenti classify smooth complex projective pairs with a nondegenerate logarithmic conformal tensor. They work in dimension at least three. When a key divisor is not nef, exactly one of three cases occurs. Either the boundary is empty and the space is a quadric. Or the space is projective space with a hyperplane boundary. Or the pair admits a negative elementary contraction generated by minimal rational curves with conformal degree one. Further cases split by the contraction target and fibre shape.
arxiv-2604-16715: Lin and colleagues introduce a training framework for graph transformers, adapting parallelization to graph structure and hardware. Graph foundation models adapt well, but implementations run on single GPUs, causing long training or memory exhaustion. Full-graph training is hard, since efficiency hinges on graph structure, bandwidth and memory capacity. With distributed sparse operations, it accelerates sparse graph attention three point eight times and cuts memory use by 78 percent. On large benchmarks, it reaches 6 times speedup while scaling to 8 GPUs. The work brings graph transformers closer to practical foundation models.
arxiv-2604-16915: Goswami and Deep present KIRA, a five-stage framework that extends retrieval-augmented question answering to images, where text-heavy knowledge bases and visual queries often fail to meet. It chunks images into regions, adapts encoders to rare visual concepts, retrieves across modalities, reasons across several hops, and checks answers against visual evidence, scoring 0.97 retrieval precision in tests across four specialized domains.
arxiv-2604-17215: Bach and three colleagues investigate which training samples cause safety drift when language models adapt continually to new tasks. High-gradient samples drive greater safety degradation and pull models toward pretrained distributions, while moderate-gradient samples enable task learning with minimal alignment loss. Their gradient-based sample selection filters high-gradient samples during fine-tuning, substantially improving alignment preservation while keeping task performance competitive, without curated safe data or architectural changes. The method proves robust across selection ratios, task orderings, and diverse attack benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-17515: Njiki and five colleagues test how hybrid quantum neural networks, which mix quantum circuits with classical learning, survive realistic hardware noise. They fold three mitigation tricks into training runs built with PennyLane and simulated under Qiskit noise models. The tricks are zero-noise extrapolation, dynamical decoupling, and layerwise Richardson extrapolation. Probabilistic error cancellation is tested separately. On the Iris dataset across five noise channels, performance holds up under phase-flip and phase-damping noise but drops sharply under strong depolarizing and amplitude-damping noise.
arxiv-2604-17815: Ye and five colleagues argue that language-model answers hide the intermediate choices shaping them. Users then cannot see assumptions or alternatives. Borrowing multiverse analysis from statistics, they build a system that states those conceptual decisions openly. It arranges them into a visible space of answers users can inspect and change, and checks them against domain norms. In trials spanning philosophy, AI alignment annotation, and poetry, participants said it clarified the choices behind answers and the range of options.
arxiv-2604-17915: Yiwei Zhang and seven colleagues unify autonomous driving around a single pretrained vision-language decoder, instead of separate decoders for each output type. Text, object detection, and trajectory outputs share one causal decoder, letting structured queries condition on visual context through attention. Planning joins the same decoder through trajectory queries, for stable joint training. On nuScenes open-loop tests the model reaches 0.28 L2 error and a 0.18 collision rate, with competitive NAVSIM closed-loop results and about 40 percent lower latency in fast mode.
arxiv-2604-18415: Castillo and Mujica study how initial charge distributions shape charged-particle coagulation under the Smoluchowski model. A random Monte Carlo model adds charge-based forces to the Brownian crash rule, letting charge signs and sizes speed or slow clumping. At middle times, charge variety speeds or delays growth based on the starting mix, while late times approach quasi-settled states set by net charge. Heavy-tailed Cauchy-Lorentz patterns promote faster growth than Gaussian ones, useful for aerosol, star-forming, and factory clumping models.
arxiv-2604-18715: Rahman, Barrett, and Last study the shape of Google AlphaEarth vectors, 64-number codes for land surface drawn from millions of United States samples. The shape is not flat, and its true size is far below 64. Idea directions twist as one moves across it, so adding vectors gives poor results while lookup works well. Their agent system, which answers environmental questions by lookup in an indexed vector store, beats a baseline that relies on the model alone.
arxiv-2604-18915: Das and three colleagues study mixed wet percolation on dual triangular and dual honeycomb lattices. Sites on the primal lattice are occupied with a given chance, and bonds join occupied and empty neighbours on the dual lattice. On the triangular lattice, with coordination number 6, the model behaves like ordinary site percolation. On the honeycomb lattice, with coordination number 3, it behaves like the hull of site clusters. The authors call this coordination dependent breakdown of universality rare.
arxiv-2604-19015: Fan and five colleagues introduce FedProxy, a federated tuning setup that swaps weak adapters for a strong proxy small language model. Federated tuning faces three linked problems: guarding model secrets, keeping client data private, and avoiding mixed data loss. Offsite tuning guards secrets by training only adapters, but leaves a gap to central training. FedProxy squeezes the private model into a high fidelity proxy, then runs server guided compression, interference aware merging, and training free fusion back into the model. It beats offsite tuning and nears central training scores.
arxiv-2604-19115: Wang and five colleagues run Mach-Zehnder interferometry on a two-dimensional superconducting quantum processor. By tuning which-way measurement strength, they show a photon shifting from wave-like to particle-like form. Tomography on two qubits in the two paths shows which-way measurements break entanglement and coherence and leak information outward. They derive complementarity links between entropy and fringe visibility. Steady which-way measurement during evolution produces the quantum Zeno effect, partially blocking the path with nonmonotonic purity and entropy.
arxiv-2604-19215: Lee and Haase split cuprate shifts from NMR data, using two hyperfine couplings' symmetry, one anisotropic and one isotropic, yielding two components. Upon doping, isotropic spins appear above the pseudogap point. Doping lowers the pseudogap point and grows isotropic spins. The isotropic spins' density grows nearly threefold faster above doping of about 0.2, where the pseudogap ends and both kinds turn superconducting. The pseudogap point measures coupling, suppressing shifts, not relaxation. Pairing covers kinds under three rules.
arxiv-2604-19315: Lee and colleagues ask whether test doubles written by developers, known as mocks, can improve language-model test generation. Their tool, MOCKMILL, pulls mocking details from existing tests and aims generation at components that those tests replace. Encoded stubbings and interaction expectations guide the new cases, and an iterative generate-and-repair loop keeps them executable. Tests on 10 classes from six Java projects with four language models compare the output against project tests and rival methods.
arxiv-2604-20115: Zhang and Yuan give the first generalization analysis for first-order bilevel minimax solvers. Using stability ideas, they bound generalization for three methods: single-speed stochastic gradient descent-ascent plus two variants at two speeds. Their results reveal a precise tradeoff among stability, generalization gaps, and practical settings. Broad empirical tests corroborate the theory on real bilevel minimax tasks.
arxiv-2604-20415: Kowalski and Uğurlu Kowalski show generic automorphisms of stable groups are supertight, strongly so, proving such maps exist. They settle a question linking supertight maps of projective linear groups to generic maps of the underlying field. They also give partial evidence, already hinted by Hrushovski, for the principle that fixed points are pseudofinite for generic maps of simple groups of finite Morley rank.
arxiv-2604-20515: Rocke, Hudson, Beanland, and Kermode build interatomic potentials, models of forces between atoms, for dislocations in indium phosphide, a semiconductor. They train Atomic Cluster Expansion and MACE models on density functional theory calculations and validate them against RSCAN density functional theory and potentials. Errors on partial dislocation formation energies reach at most 4 percent for new models, against 18 percent for the MACE-MPA foundation model and 42 to 50 percent for earlier bespoke potentials. Their bespoke MACE model keeps accuracy while running about five times faster than the MP0 and MPA foundation models.
arxiv-2604-20715: Xue and eight colleagues propose GeoRelight, a Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer that solves relighting and 3D shape estimation from a single photo. Relighting from one photo is ill-posed because a 2D image mixes shape, appearance, and light. Current methods use pipelines that pile up errors or ignore shape during relighting. GeoRelight works through isotropic NDC-Orthographic Depth, a distortion-free 3D model for diffusion models, and mixed synthetic and auto-labeled real data training. Solving shape and relighting jointly, GeoRelight beats step-by-step models and previous systems.
arxiv-2604-20815: Chao, Dong, Liu, Shu, and Wang study the Zarankiewicz problem for intersection hypergraphs from r families of axis-parallel boxes with prescribed directions. Their main result is a sharp dichotomy for the Zarankiewicz number. The number is either Theta of t times n to the r minus 1, or at least that times log n over log log n. The split depends only on a set-theoretic condition called 2-coherence. 2-coherence captures whether the configuration holds an underlying two-dimensional incidence structure, which gives rise to the extra polylogarithmic factor.
arxiv-2604-20915: Zhang, Zhang, Wu, Wei, and Sun propose Absorber LLM, a way to hold long context in model parameters without the memory cost of full attention. After absorbing past context, a context-free model is trained to match the original model's behavior on future text, syncing internal responses so causal effects survive. On long-context and streaming benchmarks it cuts inference memory and beats earlier parameter-as-memory baselines on accuracy.
arxiv-2604-21115: Vishnu Teja Kunde and three colleagues unify the theory of approximate message passing for complex-valued problems with denoisers that act on whole vectors at once. Lifting the problem to a real-valued system and folding it back through a canonical map gives scalar complex recursions for state evolution. Wirtinger derivatives appear in the correction term. Tests confirm the predictions and show gains over separable and real-valued rivals, with group-sparse LASSO as a showcase.
arxiv-2604-21315: Shuyue Feng, Cedric Caremel, and Yoshihiro Kawahara build TopoStyle, a tool that brings generative AI to 2.5D topology optimization, weighing structural strength against looks. Users can sketch on exported 3D parts on screen or work inside 3D modeling software with points. Masks limit optimization to chosen regions for custom needs. Tests show the tool weighs strength and looks well while making design faster through custom tweaks and iteration.
arxiv-2604-21415: Khandro K Chokyi, Abdel Nasser Tawfik, and Surajit Chattopadhyay study a non-singular cosmic bounce in Myrzakulov-type gravity with a Chaplygin gas. Via reconstruction and dynamical analysis, they find the squared trace parameter drives the bounce: for negative values, matter-geometry coupling breaks the null energy rule at high densities without exotic matter. A density limit gates the bounce, below which the universe follows a singular general-relativity path. The models stay viable, nearing a de Sitter attractor with sound speed well inside stability and causality bounds.
arxiv-2604-21515: Cramer and Friese offer Deductive ASPIC, a new way to reason with arguments. It aims to meet five rules of sound reasoning at once. These are closure, direct consistency, indirect consistency, non-interference, and crash-resistance. Older systems fail one or more of these rules when preferred semantics are used with undercuts. It joins gen-rebuttals with joint support bipolar tools and a ranking of claims, and meets all five rules. The goal is reasoning that stays sound even when claims attack each other.
arxiv-2604-21715: Ma and seven colleagues automate a slow, expert-heavy job in aerospace software: turning plain-language requirements into Linear Temporal Logic properties for safety checks. Their AeroReq2LTL system first normalises jargon through a data dictionary. It then makes time cues and logic links explicit in a template language before translation. On a real aerospace dataset, it reaches 85 percent precision and 88 percent recall, with outputs ready for existing checkers.
arxiv-2604-21915: Lin and eleven colleagues present Vista4D, a video reshooting framework that grounds input video and target cameras in a 4D point cloud. The method rebuilds the scene with the same dynamics from a different camera trajectory. A 4D point cloud with static splitting and rebuild preserves seen content and provides camera signals. Training with rebuilt multiview dynamic data adds toughness against point cloud flaws during real-world inference. Results improve 4D steadiness, camera control, and visual quality over baselines, and the method extends to scene expansion and recomposition.
arxiv-2604-22115: Reyes studies loop-induced Higgs decays into gauge bosons in Radiative Natural Supersymmetry. He redoes one-loop MSSM math for Higgs widths into a Z boson-photon pair, two photons, and two gluons, giving analytic scattering amplitudes. He zooms in on the region maximizing the h → Zγ width, checking predictions for the other Higgs channels. There the h → Zγ width reaches about 7.5 keV while matching the ATLAS measurement. The diphoton mode stays near the Standard Model value within 5 percent, and the gluon channel drops about 10 percent.
arxiv-2604-22215: Cacioli tests whether seven open-weight models produce valid spoken confidence for Type-2 sorting under bare number prompts with greedy sampling. A study gave 524 TriviaQA items to eight models under number and class prompts. All seven instruct models rated Invalid on number confidence, with mean ceiling 91.7 percent under number prompts. Class prompts did not fix validity; they harmed scores in six of seven models below 5 percent correctness. Token logprobs did not predict spoken confidence (mean R² below one-hundredth). Within the reasoning model, trace length linked in reverse with confidence.
arxiv-2604-23015: Jana and Mandal introduce the Drone-Delivery Packing Problem for last-mile logistics with drones collaborating with trucks. Parcels with delivery intervals and costs must be assigned to identical drones, with battery stations along the truck route for swapping or recharging. The goal is to use the fewest drones subject to battery budget and assignment compatibility. All three variants are NP-hard, and the authors give approximation algorithms for each, including a constant-factor algorithm without battery stations and improved factors when stations swap batteries.
arxiv-2604-23315: Chen tests a restriction on risk exposure from VaR intermediary models. Exposures shrink multiplicatively under constraints and grow additively in slack times. On FINRA debt from 1997 to 2026, calm slopes look additive, stress slopes multiplicative, and a Wald test rejects equal slopes. A test on 73 S&P 500 crashes links depth to longer recovery ratios, with medians above three for crashes past 30 percent, replicated on eight indices. Null models match price asymmetry without an exposure variable, and Chen stresses the test is consistent with, not proof of, it.
arxiv-2604-23415: Rahaman and Rahman argue that video action recognition should not treat its two input streams identically, since motion data and still frames carry different kinds of information. Their DualStreamHybrid design gives each stream its own backbone, then maps both outputs to a shared size before combining them. Across five ways of fusing the streams, cross-attention wins on the smaller video set while weighted fusion wins on the larger one.
arxiv-2604-23815: Balepur and colleagues collect DRACULA, the first dataset of user feedback on intermediate actions of deep research agents, rather than only final reports. Over five weeks, nineteen expert researchers posed queries, picked preferred actions, and judged whether reports applied them, yielding over 8,000 preferences and over 5,000 execution judgments. Judges predict user choices best from full selection history, and an intervention generating actions from past interactions wins most often in follow-ups.
arxiv-2604-24015: Hill and Morales-Trujillo test QubitQuest, three mini-games that teach the Bloch sphere, entanglement, and quantum circuits in short, graded steps. After a survey shaped the design, players took tests before and after playing, and scores rose, with players who finished more levels scoring higher. The authors read this as evidence that playful, bite-size lessons can ease beginners into quantum computing.
arxiv-2604-24215: Wang and three colleagues study stable optical-microwave squeezing in a hybrid system, where a moving part couples light and microwave modes. Modulated drives on both light modes plus a mechanical amplifier build a Hamiltonian capturing the squeezing interaction. Non-Markovian noise boosts squeezing well above the Markovian case, and squeezing can persist even without external drives, softening anti-squeezing harm. Persistence grows further when microwave and optical spectra match, giving a way to generate and keep two-mode squeezing in structured reservoirs.
arxiv-2604-24915: El Morsalani and Barkatou study the inverse problem for the return map on the boundary of a convex core. Splitting return shifts into sideways and normal parts, they derive an exact nonlinear system for thickness, yielding a single-point answer. Linearizing at fixed points introduces an operator Q-star: when Q-star is nonzero, thickness and outer shape are recoverable via global spread. When Q-star is zero, local doubt is settled with nonlinear Ehresmann-type transport plus holonomy maps on closed paths.
arxiv-2604-25215: Sheng shows exact force fields come from density functional theory variationally. Force fields are usually set in nuclear configuration space, while density functional theory uses potentials and densities. The potential-energy surface is the pullback of the external energy functional along the map from nuclear configurations to Coulomb potentials. Pulling these objects back yields the force and the nuclear Hessian, plus terms from nuclear-generated potential and nuclear-nuclear repulsion. The result places force fields, density functional theory and response theory in one derivative hierarchy, in a conceptual work.
arxiv-2604-25515: Song and Tang report relativistic many-body calculations of the Landé g-factor interelectronic-interaction correction for 2s1/2, 2p1/2, 2p3/2, and 3s1/2 in lithium-like ions. Z runs from 4 to 20. From the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian, positive-energy parts use coupled-cluster excitations, and negative-energy parts enter through third-order perturbation theory. Negative-energy states give a correction whose size and sign vary with Z and the state. For 2p1/2, it reaches 30 percent of the total at Z equal to 20. Agreement with calculations is better than 0.1 percent, confirming reliability.
arxiv-2604-25715: Stenger, Hellberg, and Gunlycke compute ground-state energies of Ising models using samples from a quantum computer running a cascaded variational eigensolver with a guided-sampling ansatz, on up to 63 qubits. They study a heavy-hex lattice matched to the hardware layout, covering homogeneous and random-coupling models. The work maps where acceptable quantum errors end as qubit count and coupling strength vary, and adds entropic and subspace analyses. The subspace results suggest the Ising model suits near-term quantum hardware especially well.
arxiv-2604-25815: Belhadjoudja and Morris map the region of attraction for a backstepping observer on the one-dimensional quasilinear heat equation. Linear design methods work locally for nonlinear systems, but not the attraction region or results versus gains. Their design comes from the linear heat model with constant diffusivity, treating that system as a perturbation of it. They prove exponential stability of the estimation error, with that region set by gains and diffusivity mismatch. The error reaches zero rather than merely a mismatch-scaled neighborhood, even though it persists.
arxiv-2604-26115: Fernández Ouaridi builds a structure theory for transposed Poisson algebras over fields of characteristic not two. The paper proves every finite-dimensional example over an algebraically closed field splits as a direct sum of a unital ideal and a nilpotent ideal. That restricts simple cases and yields a full classification above characteristic three. There, every simple algebra has a Zassenhaus algebra as its Lie algebra and belongs to a mutated family. The isomorphism problem and unital irreducible representations are also settled, with uses in several nearby structures.
arxiv-2604-26315: Saha, writing for the Belle II collaboration, laid out an amplitude analysis of B decays to a kaon and two pions plus a photon. The time-dependent CP asymmetry in that channel can reveal physics beyond the Standard Model, but only if decays through CP-eigenstate kaon resonances are separated from the rest. The analysis distinguishes those paths so the measurement can be turned into a clean constraint on new physics.
arxiv-2604-26415: Liu studied quotients of numerical semigroups. Such a set is built by keeping whole numbers whose multiples by a fixed integer land in the starting set. The quotient itself is again a numerical semigroup. He first mapped the Apéry set for a class of such quotients, then worked out half-closed formulas for their Frobenius number and genus under certain conditions. For hand-picked parameter values, fully explicit Frobenius formulas followed. The work carries the classical Frobenius problem into quotient semigroups.
arxiv-2604-26615: Hasanli and five colleagues built an AI-native test-driven development frame that turns TDD discipline into firm rules for multi-agent code generation. Large language models speed coding but waver in stability, determinism, and discipline when free, and existing methods treat tests as side inputs rather than constraints. Their layered design writes rules into a machine-readable manifesto spread across planning, generation, repair, and validation, splitting model proposals from engine control. Phase order, bounded repair loops, check gates, and atomic mutation control improve stability and repeat runs.
arxiv-2604-26915: Gonzalez and forty-four colleagues use DESI Data Release 1 to test whether gravity deviates from general relativity at a new scale. Linking a Yukawa-like potential to the Hu-Sawicki f(R) model, they bound a hypothetical fifth force from a massive scalar field. They find no deviation from general relativity, capping log10 |f_R0| below negative 4.59 at 95 percent confidence, or a force range under 18 megaparsecs. Adding DESI BAO data or other probes barely moves the results, and the modified-gravity parameters show little degeneracy with neutrino masses.
arxiv-2604-27015: Kumar and four colleagues present a swap-free routing framework for qudits on near-neighbor hardware, where connectivity makes nonlocal gates expensive. Higher qudit levels act as orthogonal spectral buses carrying control information without moving the state. A nonlocal operation over a path of length L needs 2L plus 1 routing primitives, against a 3L baseline. Overlapping routes stay distinct via bus labels in the same qudits. The algebra extends to Boolean fan-in at one target, with controls triggering a local unitary from any Boolean function of bus digits.
arxiv-2604-27115: Siam and seven colleagues probe neuron pruning in language models tuned for math reasoning and code writing, asking whether some neurons matter far more than others for one task. They rank neurons by an activation-based selectivity score, cut low-scoring ones while holding task accuracy, and beat random cutting. Cutting the highest-scoring few instead shows how a small set can carry the task, and how far a pruned model can recover.
arxiv-2604-27315: Kimura-Ida asks whether multi-language sentence vectors support meaningful cross-language comparison of research funding projects. Such comparison matters more for science policy and planning. Language differences block it. KAKENHI descriptions are mainly Japanese, while NSF, NIH, and UKRI projects are documented in English. For each KAKENHI project she builds two versions. One is the original Japanese text. The other is its machine-made English version. Both are embedded in a shared meaning space with multilingual Sentence-BERT, and she tests how translation shifts meaning.
arxiv-2604-27415: Li and six colleagues present ChipLingo, a training pipeline that adapts large language models to electronic design automation, a knowledge-heavy, document-driven field. Its three stages build a domain corpus, pretrain adaptively, and align instructions with retrieval scenario training. ChipLingo 8B scores 59.7 percent on their EDA-Bench benchmark, beating the same-scale model and some larger general models, while ChipLingo 32B reaches about 70 percent, near leading closed-source models. Question-answer augmentation helps domain performance, and retrieval scenario training limits the usual post-training drop in retrieval use.
arxiv-2604-27815: Akhond and three colleagues build Newman-Penrose and Aretakis charges for D3-branes and D3-brane bound states in D=10, D=4, and D=5. They match the two sets with care. A flat space in D=4 maps, by Couch-Torrence inversion, to the shape near an extremal horizon. With the intact supersymmetry of Type IIB supergravity, they tie dilaton charges to higher spin charges. They work out endless towers of saved far-field spinor charges from dilatino wiggles and their inversion map.
arxiv-2604-27915: Ng and nine colleagues build Affinity Tailor, a scheduler keeping workloads near cached data, not scattered across cores. Spread work loses cache, predictor, and prefetcher reuse, and hard partitions waste capacity, so compact demand-sized sets serve as hints, not walls. A user-space controller sizes each set to demand, keeping sets apart and inside few cache domains. The kernel lets threads spill over when needed. At Google it lifts per-CPU throughput 12 percent on chiplet machines and 3 percent elsewhere over Linux CFS, plus 3 to 7 percent per gigabyte.
arxiv-2604-28015: Chen proves that two rank-two Drinfeld modules without complex multiplication give the same Galois representation if their Frobenius traces match at every place bar finitely many. The proof widens to Galois representations over local fields of positive characteristic when they admit no smaller invariant parts. He also proves the strong multiplicity one property in function-field form.
arxiv-2604-28115: Jiang and colleagues present FreeOcc, a training-free system that predicts which voxels are occupied, and with what meaning, from ordinary or depth camera sequences. Without 3D labels, pose truth or any training stage, it chains SLAM poses, dense Gaussian maps and vision-language semantics into voxels through a probabilistic projection. It more than doubles overlap scores over prior self-supervised methods on an indoor benchmark. It also transfers zero-shot to new rooms, alongside a new ReplicaOcc benchmark.
arxiv-2605-00015:
Siyang Li and six co-authors present TimeRFT, a reinforcement learning method for adapting time series foundation models. These pretrained models forecast well and use data efficiently, but adapting them to new tasks is hard: time series shift over time, and supervised fine-tuning overfits, especially when downstream data are scarce. The authors replace that fine-tuning with a reinforcement approach built for forecasting.

TimeRFT adds two recipes. A quality-aware temporal reward scores how each prediction step contributes to the whole forecast, giving fine-grained credit. A difficulty-aware selection strategy favors informative samples with patterns that generalize. Across diverse real-world forecasting benchmarks and data regimes, TimeRFT beats supervised adaptation in accuracy and holds up better when the distribution shifts unexpectedly.
arxiv-2605-00315:
Hao Li and Steffen Knoblauch write an opinion paper on responsible GeoAI, AI that works with location data, used to map extreme weather and disasters. Such mapping can cut risk faster as floods, fires, and storms grow more frequent. But a purely results-driven rollout, they argue, can widen gaps between places and mislead rescue choices.

The authors unpack it along four linked axes: who is covered, whether the system can explain itself, whether the practice can last, and ethics, each shown through disaster mapping cases. The cost to the planet of the computing itself counts among the concerns. They then propose a model of shared rules that sorts the work into three scopes: data, use, and society. Their closing appeal asks the wider mapping community to build shared rules, not just better code.
arxiv-2605-00615:
The CMS Collaboration reports the first observation of a rare decay of the eta meson, in which it transforms into a muon pair plus an electron pair. The result comes from proton-proton collisions at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, using data gathered in 2022 with a high-rate trigger that watches for dimuon events. Such rare decays test the Standard Model's account of how mesons decay through virtual photons.

To measure the decay's frequency, the team normalizes against a better-known eta decay into a muon pair and a photon. The branching fraction they find is a few parts per million, with an uncertainty of about a third of the value. That figure sits close to one hundred times below the previous experimental limit. It also agrees with recent theoretical predictions, which is why a first observation at exactly this level counts as a clean confirmation rather than a surprise.
arxiv-2605-01015:
Amirreza Rouhi, Vishal Kumar, Wen Wu, Melissa Kozul, and Oriol Lehmkuhl propose unstructured grids to cut the cost of direct numerical simulations of wall turbulence. Their eta-grid sets wall-normal and spanwise grid sizes in proportion to the local Kolmogorov scale, the smallest turbulent scale. An inner layer near the wall keeps conventional fine spacing, while above it spacing follows the local scale.

The framework is tested with finite volume and spectral element solvers on channel flows and boundary layers over smooth walls and riblets, up to moderately high Reynolds numbers. Turbulence statistics and energy spectra differ from conventional Cartesian grid results by less than one percent. The grid point count scales more favorably as Reynolds number grows, offering substantial savings.
arxiv-2605-01115:
R. Weht, A. A. Aligia, and M. Nunez-Regueiro study band structure in graphite stackings that combine different rhombohedral orders, motivated by indications of high-temperature superconductivity in natural graphite enriched in the rhombohedral phase. Using first-principles calculations, they examine configurations that mix graphite structures and reverse the rhombohedral sequence. The focus is whether flat bands, where electron energy barely varies, emerge near the Fermi level.

When the two different rhombohedral orderings are combined, flat bands of topological origin appear at the interface between the two domains, near special points of the Brillouin zone. A simple tight-binding model mapped onto a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain gives a transparent physical explanation of why those interface bands arise.
arxiv-2605-01215:
José Gregorio Rodríguez-Nieto, Olga Patricia Salazar-Díaz, Andrés Sarrazola-Alzate, and Raúl Velásquez prove a cohomological version of Maschke's theorem for generalized digroups, algebraic structures that extend groups. Maschke-type results concern when representations split into simpler pieces. For a generalized digroup, the authors construct an associative enveloping algebra and prove its representation category is equivalent to the category of left modules over that algebra.

Under a Maschke-type condition on the group component, short exact sequences split on one side. The obstruction to full splitting is described by cocycles and identified with an Ext group between the relevant representations. A spectral sequence is also derived, with consequences for splitting behavior and for cases where semisimplicity fails.
arxiv-2605-01315:
Abit Ahmad Oktarian and five co-authors investigate sentiment classification of Steam game reviews with an attention-based bidirectional LSTM model. Their dataset samples tens of thousands of reviews from a larger Steam corpus. A traditional baseline using TF-IDF features with automated machine learning is compared against a deep learning approach implemented in PyTorch, trained to address class imbalance in the review labels.

The BiLSTM with attention model, trained with class-weighted loss, achieves solid accuracy and weighted F-score on the test set, with high recall for negative reviews. Attention visualizations highlight sentiment-bearing words, adding interpretability to the predictions. The authors conclude the model is effective for analyzing player sentiment and useful for helping developers understand player feedback at scale.
arxiv-2605-01715:
Sushil Bikhchandani and Debasis Mishra design job matching rules that firms and workers cannot game. Each firm can hire many workers and each worker takes one job. Firms' values for bundles of workers are public, while each worker's dislike of each firm is private. The mechanism must make honesty best while keeping both sides willing to take part.

The classic VCG mechanism is known to be the only one that is strategy-proof, efficient, and safe for workers, but it can leave a firm worse off than walking away. The pair show VCG is safe for firms exactly when firm values obey a weak substitutes condition, a limit on how workers crowd each other out. Strengthen the demand so no firm wants to fire anyone it was assigned, and the condition becomes submodularity of firm values. The results draw a clean line around when the canonical mechanism respects participation.
arxiv-2605-01915:
André Chatel and colleagues work on sensing very cold temperatures with superconducting microwave resonators. Such sensors use little power and can be sharp below ten kelvin, which suits complex cryogenic systems. The team asks whether cutting fine trenches into the surface of a niobium-titanium film can make a resonator respond more strongly to temperature.

They pattern trench arrays on the inductive line of a planar resonator and partly etch the film to shift its transition point. The shift lowered that point by about one and a half kelvin and raised temperature sensitivity tenfold, though it also added microwave loss. The best device reached a strong response at 4.2 kelvin with the widest trenches.
arxiv-2605-02015:
Yan Zhou and colleagues make intrusion detection lighter by splitting a hard learning problem into smaller parts. Network traffic is high-dimensional, noisy, and imbalanced, so strong detectors tend to be large and hard to run on small devices. Their divide-and-conquer method uses correlations in the data to form focused subtasks for simple models.

Decision trees trained on those subtasks reached up to about forty-three percent higher local accuracy in their tests. Model size fell by as much as two hundred fifty-seven times on real intrusion data sets. The authors also report better robustness against attacks and clearer explanations, both of which matter when a detector must run at the edge.
arxiv-2605-02115:
Connor Bass introduces geometric categories in higher category theory. The main example is an infinity-topos. The paper studies sheaves on such categories. Sheaves glue local data into global data. Bass shows they are marked by a form of descent, in both plain and hyper forms.

As a use, Bass studies sheaves on topoi at each truncation level. The effective epimorphism topology there is shown to be the canonical topology. For finite levels, sheaves match truncated sheaves on certain infinity-topoi. The study then widens to sheaves on the category of all infinity-topoi. An appendix treats modules under a reflective monoidal functor, and how sheaf formation behaves when the setting changes.
arxiv-2605-02215:
Fazle Rabbi and Jinqiu Yang build HEJ-Robust, a benchmark that tests whether language models can repair buggy code when the code's form changes but its meaning does not. Standard repair tests use one canonical form of each bug, so robustness to the syntactic variation found in real software goes unmeasured. The authors start from HumanEval-Java-Bug and apply eight meaning-preserving transformations.

That process yields 1,450 transformed instances. Five fine-tuned models were tested on the set. Performance fell by more than half under several transformations, a sharp drop for changes that should not alter what the code does. The result suggests current repair models rely on surface form more than on program meaning.
arxiv-2605-02315:
Christine Little and Daniel Kosov develop a theory of dispersion interactions between two nanostructures driven out of equilibrium by a voltage. Dispersion forces, such as the London attraction, are usually treated at equilibrium. Here each nanostructure is an open quantum system held in a nonequilibrium steady state by an applied bias, using nonequilibrium Green's function methods.

Starting from a two-particle Green's function, they derive the interaction energy from each system's polarisation propagators. The energy splits cleanly into charge noise and charge dissipation parts, a fluctuation-dissipation reading that generalises the equilibrium picture. Model calculations on coupled molecular junctions show voltage can raise the attractive interaction by nearly tenfold. At equilibrium, the interaction stays universally attractive in their result.
arxiv-2605-02415:
Jonathan Leon Schubert reports recent results from NA62, a fixed-target kaon experiment at the CERN SPS, in both kaon and beam-dump modes. In kaon mode, NA62 measured the ultra-rare decay of a charged kaon to a pion plus a neutrino-antineutrino pair, using data collected from 2016 to 2024. The measurement agrees with past results and with the Standard Model.

In beam-dump mode, the experiment searched for new-physics particles with masses from about 150 to 2,000 mega-electronvolts, using dedicated runs from 2021 to 2024. The search targeted decays expected for heavy neutral leptons, to a hadron plus a lepton. No event was observed in any signal channel, so upper limits were set on coupling to Standard Model particles.
arxiv-2605-02715:
Sandra Arcos-Holzinger and three co-authors probe how disturbances deform the inner geometry of self-supervised speech models. Such models perform well on later tasks, yet their learned representations are poorly understood under natural and hostile perturbations. Older studies compared whole representations or used global size measures, missing local changes.

Their framework tracks local intrinsic dimensionality, layer by layer, in two leading speech models. Under quiet, noisy conditions this local size rises for all perturbations. At cleaner signal levels the paths split: benign noise settles back toward the clean profile, while hostile inputs keep early layers inflated. The inflation appears alongside worse transcription, and layer-wise measures detect anomalies with strong scores. Transcript-free monitoring of deployed speech models is the stated aim.
arxiv-2605-02815:
Quang Hieu Pham and seven co-authors present FlexSQL, an agent that turns written questions into database queries over large analytical stores. The work demands browsing complex schemas, resolving vague wording, and grounding choices in real data. Most systems fetch schema parts once at the start and revisit the database only to repair errors, so early mistakes are hard to escape.

FlexSQL can explore schema, inspect values, and run check queries at any point in its reasoning. It drafts several execution plans to cover different readings of a question, writes each in SQL or Python as fits, and repairs at two levels, from code fixes up to revised plans. On a hard benchmark it beat strong open baselines that used larger models, and as a skill inside a general coding agent it lifted scores further.
arxiv-2605-03015:
